questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that parking is not allowed in this area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: When turning left at a green light, you must yield to oncoming traffic. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are about to become one lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: When a lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, this hand signal means the group should stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up. Be prepared to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: When your left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, this hand signal means you plan to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign tells you to slow down at the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to allow them to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
The road ahead winds a series of turns or curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pavement is wet, reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Slow down and increase the distance between your vehicle and others. Avoid sudden braking or quick direction changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The group will pull off at the next exit.

questions.explanation: When the lead rider raises their left arm and extends their index finger, it signals the group to form a single line.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the safest speed to travel when exiting a highway. The number shown is the recommended maximum speed for that exit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on an upcoming hill.
There are trucks on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill or downgrade is coming ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This hand signal tells other riders in the group to follow you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Driving with your headlights out of alignment because one side of your car is higher than the other.
Damaging a tire from drifting onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning, if the shoulder has water on it.
Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the shoulder is lower than the road. If a wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not brake hard or steer sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are permitted on an upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead is wide enough for only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts drivers that an upcoming bridge is narrow. You may not have enough space to pass or meet a truck. Proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer often cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means "Yield." Slow down and check for traffic. Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and other vehicles. Stop only if necessary.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are used only to mark no passing zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals. A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two-way traffic is coming ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends or roadway narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low overpass ahead. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (in this case, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their left arm straight out with palm facing down and swings their arm down to their side, the following riders should slow down.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.
Come to a full stop, then proceed if it is safe to do so.
Proceed carefully through the intersection, but you may not always need to stop.
Stop only for traffic on an intersecting road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then proceed if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop. Then proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the road ahead will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield just to the traffic on the right.
Yield just to the traffic on the left.
Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic go first before you enter the intersection or roadway.
